validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION well confirmed, not a phantom or misclassified row. RH Energytrans LLC (Erie, PA; an EmKey Energy LLC affiliate) filed a FERC application Oct 2017 to build a new INTERSTATE gas transmission pipeline (Riseberg/Risberg Line): construction began early 2019, FERC authorized start-of-service ~Dec 1 2019, and it is described as running/delivering gas by Dec 2019 onward. Independent, non-GEM confirmation across 6+ distinct origins: RH Energytrans's own project microsite (rhenergytrans.com/learn-more/); Pipeline News/PGJ's Oct-2018 Planned Projects PDF; Marcellus Drilling News (two separate dated articles, Dec 2018 and Dec 2019); Ohio River Corridor (trade group, June 2019); GoErie.com/Erie Times-News (Aug 2019, on-the-ground reporting with named company officials Dennis Holbrook and Kyle Rhoades quoted). No duplicate in the 46-row roster (unique Meadville PA-to-Ashtabula Co OH route, no other row plausibly the same pipe). Classification (Fuel=Gas, FERC-jurisdictional interstate transmission, not gathering) matches every source -- RH is explicit that this converts EXISTING gathering pipe (bought from EmKey Gathering) to natural-gas TRANSMISSION service, exactly the GEM PipelineType this row should carry. Length (28 mi), Diameter (12 in), Capacity (55 MMcf/d), StartYear (2019), Operator/Owner (RH Energytrans, 100%) all corroborate the current sheet values -- see fills[] for the added refs. Three real defects found and detailed as separate concern entries below: SegmentCost ($88M on the sheet vs. a unanimous $86M across every independent source), ConstructionMonth (June on the sheet vs. construction actually breaking ground Jan/Feb 2019 per two independent contemporaneous sources), and a granularity mismatch between the recorded 28-mi LengthKnown (new-build only) and the recorded StartPrefecture/District='Crawford County' (which is the origin of the full 60-mi corridor, not the 28-mi new segment). Opened all 9 of the row's harvested wiki citations. fractracker.org's national map (cite_note-ftmap-2) never names Risberg and is not usable as a ref for this row (generic aggregate map, fails the name-the-pipeline test) -- noted, not treated as an existence flag given how much independent naming evidence exists elsewhere. eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php (cite_note-eia-4) is a navigational hub, not an article -- also unusable directly; did not chase the underlying EIA workbook given time budget and the strength of other sourcing. gascompressionmagazine.com's live article (cite_note-5) 403s to the verifier's default UA (bot-wall) -- confirmed manually with a browser UA (200, full FERC-EA-derived text matches the pipeline name and every disputed figure) and cited via its 2018-07-15 Wayback capture instead, which passes url_verifier cleanly.

GEM records SegmentCost=88,000,000 USD. Every independent source that states a project cost says $86 million, not $88 million: RH Energytrans's own site ('Early estimates place the project costs at approximately $86,000,000'); Marcellus Drilling News, Dec 11 2018 ('Risberg is a 60-mile, $86 million pipeline'); Marcellus Drilling News, Dec 2 2019 ('Risberg cost roughly $86 million to build'); Ohio River Corridor, June 12 2019 ('the $86 million pipeline'); GoErie.com/Erie Times-News, Aug 28 2019 ('the $86 million Risberg Pipeline'). That is 4 independent origins (developer + 3 separate press outlets) spanning 2018-2019, all landing on the identical $86M figure with no source anywhere stating $88M. This is not a rounding or currency-unit issue -- it is a flat disagreement with the sheet. Recommend correcting SegmentCost to 86000000.00 USD.

validity.recommendation: verify and likely correct ConstructionMonth away from June (candidate: January; ConstructionYear=2019 is confirmed correct)
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records ConstructionYear=2019 / ConstructionMonth=6 (June). ConstructionYear=2019 is solidly confirmed (multiple sources describe active/ongoing construction throughout 2019). But ConstructionMonth=June is contradicted by two independent, dated, contemporaneous sources describing when ground was actually broken: GoErie.com/Erie Times-News (Aug 28 2019, quoting company officials) states 'construction, which began with clearing land in January, is moving toward completion' -- i.e. January 2019. Marcellus Drilling News's Dec 2 2019 recap instead says the pipeline 'began construction in February' -- i.e. February 2019. Both disagree with each other on the exact month (Jan vs Feb) but both clearly disagree with the sheet's June, and June is also inconsistent with the Ohio River Corridor article's June 12 2019 headline 'Construction on Risberg Line pipeline begins' -- read in full, that article says construction 'has finally reached Ohio' by June 2019, i.e. it describes construction progress reaching the Ohio end of the route months after the PA-side ground-breaking, not the overall start date. Given the conflict between the two candidate months, I lead with January (the more detailed, directly-quoted, on-the-ground GoErie account) but flag the Jan/Feb disagreement rather than asserting either with full confidence -- a human should resolve the exact month against the FERC docket's notice-to-proceed filing if precision below the year matters.

validity.recommendation: verify whether StartPrefecture/District should read Erie County (matching the recorded 28-mi new-build LengthKnown) rather than Crawford County (which matches the full 60-mi corridor, of which only 28 mi is the new pipe this row's length actually counts)
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's LengthKnown=28.00 mi matches every source's figure for the NEW-BUILD portion only: RH Energytrans's own site ('approximately 16 miles of new pipeline...in Pennsylvania and approximately 12 miles of new pipeline...in Ohio' = 28 mi new); Pipeline News/PGJ PDF ('Length: 28 miles'); the gascompressionmagazine/FERC-EA article, twice ('28 miles (45 km) of new 12-in.-diameter pipeline' / 'construction of an additional 28 miles of new 12-inch pipeline'). But those same sources describe the FULL corridor -- new-build plus 32 mi of purchased, converted existing gathering pipe -- as running from Meadville/Crawford County, PA (where the existing pipe being converted begins, at an interconnect with Tennessee Gas Pipeline) through Erie County, PA, into Ashtabula County, OH -- a 60-mile total (Marcellus Drilling News, twice: 'a 60-mile...pipeline from Crawford County, PA through Erie County and into Ashtabula County, OH'). GoErie.com is explicit that the 28-mile NEW-BUILD segment itself -- the same mileage the sheet's LengthKnown records -- runs 'connecting Elk Creek Township in Erie County with North Kingsville' (Ashtabula Co, OH), i.e. the new pipe begins in Erie County, not Crawford County. So the row's LengthKnown (28 mi, new-build only) and its StartPrefecture/District (Crawford County, the origin of the full 60-mi corridor) currently describe two different physical extents of the same nominal project -- a classic aggregate-vs-segment mismatch. EndPrefecture/District (Ashtabula County) and both StartState/Province='Pennsylvania' / EndState/Province='Ohio' are solidly confirmed by every source and are NOT in question. Recommend a human decide whether this row is meant to represent the 28-mi new-build segment (in which case StartPrefecture/District should be Erie County) or the full 60-mi corridor (in which case LengthKnown would need to become 60 and Diameter would need to become a multi-value '8, 12' to match the mixed existing+new pipe) -- but do not just paste one figure onto the other without picking a consistent scope.
